correctness.rationale: Exact Lucas-submask parity and the symmetric-difference lower bound give |E f(s)f(t)| <= rho^(2^(h(t)-1)) for s<t; summing by bit counts yields G(2^L) <= exp(C(log(L+2))^2). Dyadic decomposition yields E max_prefix^2 <= 2^L exp(C(log(L+2))^2); Markov and dyadic Borel-Cantelli give an almost-sure near-root-N spatial maximal bound. Geometric(1/2) occupation times, a Doob inequality for their centered weighted sums, and a geometric-tail bound transfer this to the complete bootstrap cross-bracket. Fair beta bits transform invertibly into iid signs; the renewal-reward CLT gives a nondegenerate annealed N(0,3) limit, proving that a smaller universal polynomial exponent is impossible. The actual standalone checker passed 10,912 exact finite assertions.

value.rationale: The entire quenched predictable cross-bracket is quantitatively controlled at the Brownian-square-root exponent uniformly for arbitrary nonstationary elliptic static coefficient profiles. This is a natural strong rate needed in finite-horizon martingale covariance estimates and is not implied by mere quenched Cesaro convergence. Fair-bit fluctuations prove that the universal polynomial exponent is exactly best possible. The result is a reusable binary-submask maximal estimate beyond a routine scalar finite calculation.
